fields.name: Anaṅgabhīmadeva II
fields.place: Purī (Orissa): the temple of Jagannātha (completed 1197), Vimalā and Lakṣmī; the Nārāyaṇa-chātā maṭha
fields.notes: King of Orissa of the Gaṅgā dynasty; completed the present temple of Jagannātha begun by Coḍagaṅgadeva (edict of 1119 Śaka, 1197), with its rampart and the temples of Vimalā and Lakṣmī; installed Śubha-lakṣmī-nārāyaṇa near the Baḍa-daṇḍa; gave many land grants for Jagannātha's worship (Gaṅgā-vaṁśānucarita).

fields.disappearance: Kept on Makara-saṅkrānti at Bāḍaṅgañj (the record's text)
fields.place: Bāḍaṅgañj (Goghāṭ, Hooghly); Kāndrā; samādhis at Bāḍaṅgañj, Gokulnagar (Viṣṇupura) and Sonāmukhī (Bankura); Vṛndāvana (1735)
fields.notes: A long-lived saint «many years after Lord Caitanya»: left Bāḍaṅgañj for Vṛndāvana on 17 Pauṣa 1657 Śaka (1735); remains enshrined at three places; many disciples; taught religion in the village schools. Said to be a mantra-disciple of Jāhnavā Mātā and a childhood friend of Jñānadāsa of Kāndrā; moved Vipra Paraśurāma to take veśa. (These dates and links do not fit together.)

fields.works: Āmukta-mālyadā (Viṣṇucittīya), in Telugu; other works in Telugu and Sanskrit
fields.notes: King of Vijayanagara; after invading Pratāparudra's kingdom, married his daughter Jaganmohinī-devī (Tukkā) with the land south of the Kṛṣṇā as dowry. Patron of the arts; wrote the Āmukta-mālyadā, the story of the girl who offered the Lord the garlands she had worn and married Him at Śrīraṅgam.
